nodes.name: Get Active Search Criteria
nodes.notes: Deliberately NO onError/continueRegularOutput here, unlike every other Airtable node in this workflow - if this fails, the run should visibly fail rather than silently look identical to 'zero active criteria rows this week'.

nodes.name: Search Google - LinkedIn Profiles
nodes.notes: First live test (execution 90) got 'Google hasn't returned any results for this query' with a quoted location phrase added on top of site: + quoted role - too restrictive. Dropped the quoted phrase, but execution 94 then showed the real cost: with no location word in the query text at all, SerpApi's location API parameter alone doesn't filter results by location (it only biases where the search is simulated from) - a globally prominent but wrong-location person got pulled in for a London search. Fixed by re-adding location as an UNQUOTED keyword. v2: this lane is now demoted to a low-priority/supplementary source rather than primary - the company-first (Phase B') and editorial-mention (Phase B'') lanes carry more weight, since this one produced usable results in only ~1 of 4 live tests.

nodes.name: Search Google - Companies
nodes.notes: v2: repurposed from a 'directory listing' search into a company-discovery search - aims at real company websites (fed into the new fetch+extract stage) rather than directory listing pages. Query intentionally unquoted (see sibling nodes' notes on execution 90's over-quoting causing zero results).

parameters.name: q
parameters.value: ={{$('Normalize Criteria Row').item.json.role_keywords}} {{$('Normalize Criteria Row').item.json.location}} (interview OR profile OR "meet the" OR award OR speaker) -site:linkedin.com -site:instagram.com -site:tiktok.com -site:facebook.com

nodes.name: Search Google - Editorial Mentions
nodes.notes: v2: repurposed from a generic catch-all into a third-party/editorial-mention search - looks for a named person mentioned by someone other than their own employer (profile pieces, award/speaker listings, association directories). Added to mitigate the gap where a real prospect has a strong public presence but their employer's own site never names them - see plan doc / README for full rationale. gl (country) param added 2026-08-01, same reason as Search Google - Companies. Social platform exclusions added 2026-08-01 after execution 101 matched an irrelevant Instagram Reel purely because it contained the literal phrase 'meet the' - social platforms trend toward influencer content, not genuine third-party business profile pieces.

nodes.name: Tag Source - LinkedIn
nodes.notes: Bakes criteria fields in as literal data (via explicit node reference) before the fan-out/merge, rather than relying on cross-node lookups surviving the Merge node later.

options.systemMessage:
You are a lead-prospecting research assistant. You will be given a search result (title, URL, snippet) PLUS the full visible text of the page at that URL, if it could be fetched, plus a target location this search was meant to find prospects in. The source_type tells you what kind of page this is: 'LinkedIn' (a Google-indexed LinkedIn snippet, often thin), 'CompanySite' (a company's own website - look for an About/Team/Leadership section in the page text), or 'EditorialMention' (a third-party page - press/interview/profile/award/directory listing - that names someone independent of their own employer).

The result may or may not represent a real, relevant business contact. Extract prospect details ONLY when clearly supported by the text - never invent or guess a name, title, or company. Prefer the full page text over the snippet when both are present; the snippet is often too thin to extract from reliably.

Target audience for this whole system: SMB (small-to-medium business) leadership - founders, owners, directors, and department heads - NOT junior/individual-contributor roles and NOT large-enterprise contacts. Only extract prospect_name if the page ITSELF names a specific individual WITH a title (do not infer someone exists from context - e.g. do not assume 'the founder' is a specific extractable name unless the page states it) - and prefer names whose title matches a founder/owner/director/head-of level role consistent with the criteria's role keywords.

Rules:
- prospect_name: a specific named individual's full name, ONLY if one is identifiable in the title/snippet/page text. LinkedIn results are usually formatted 'FirstName LastName - Title - Company | LinkedIn' - parse that pattern. If the result is a directory listing, a company page with no named leadership, or has no named individual at all, set this to null.
- prospect_title: the person's job title/role if stated, else null.
- company_name: the company/organization name if identifiable, else null.
- company_website: a company website URL if one is visible in the text (the URL itself, if source_type is CompanySite, or a company site mentioned in an EditorialMention page), else null.
- linkedin_url: the exact URL verbatim, ONLY if source_type is LinkedIn and the URL matches a linkedin.com/in/ profile pattern, else null.
- location: a location if stated in the snippet or page text, else null.
- LOCATION CHECK (important): compare the stated location (if any) against the target location given above. If the text clearly places the person/company somewhere unrelated (a different country, or a distant city with no stated connection to the target area), this is very likely the WRONG match for this search - even if they look prominent or authoritative. In that case, still extract what the text says, but set needs_manual_review=true and explain the mismatch in review_reason. Do not silently treat a globally famous but geographically mismatched result as a good match.
- PLACE-NAME AMBIGUITY (important): some target locations are also common surnames or match unrelated places in other countries (e.g. 'Bristol' is a UK city AND a surname AND several US towns - Bristol, Tennessee/Virginia/Connecticut/Rhode Island; this kind of collision applies to many place names, not just this one). If the target location word's only appearance is inside a person's surname or a company/brand name - not as an actual geographic reference - that is NOT a genuine location match. Check real context instead: an address, a postcode/zip format, a phone number's country code, a currency symbol, or other place names mentioned nearby. If context points to a different country than the target, treat this exactly like a LOCATION CHECK mismatch (needs_manual_review=true), regardless of whether the target location word happens to appear in the text.
- confidence: your own 0-1 confidence that this result represents a real, useful, LOCATION-APPROPRIATE, SMB-LEADERSHIP-APPROPRIATE prospect for outreach - lower this for a location mismatch, a non-leadership role, or an enterprise-scale company even if the name/title extraction itself is clear.
- needs_manual_review: true if prospect_name is null, confidence is below 0.5, location clearly mismatches the target, or the result looks unrelated/spam.
- review_reason: a short explanation when needs_manual_review is true, else empty string.

Respond only with the required JSON output - never fabricate data you cannot support from the given text.

("OR({Source URL} = '" + $('Limit Results Per Criteria Row').item.json.prospect_source_link + "', {LinkedIn URL} = '" + $('Prospect Extraction Agent').item.json.output.linkedin_url + "')") : ("{Source URL} = '" + $('Limit Results Per Criteria Row').item.json.prospect_source_link + "'") }}

nodes.name: Dedup Check - Existing Prospect
nodes.notes: Primary dedup key (Source URL) is captured before the Agent ran, so an Agent failure can't corrupt this check. LinkedIn URL is OR'd in only when the Agent actually produced one - never blindly OR'd against a possibly-blank field. alwaysOutputData=true because Airtable Search returns zero items (not one empty item) on no match, which would otherwise starve the downstream IF node.

value.Location: ={{$('Normalize Agent Output').item.json.location || $('Limit Results Per Criteria Row').item.json.criteria_location}}

nodes.name: Create Prospect - Needs Review
nodes.notes: Skips Dropcontact entirely - no reliable name/company to enrich against, and it saves enrichment API credits.

nodes.name: Enrich Contact - Dropcontact
nodes.notes: simplify=true returns a request_id immediately rather than waiting per-item; a shared Wait node downstream pays the async delay once per batch, not once per prospect. v2: this now runs as a fallback after Hunter's emailFinder comes up empty, not as the only enrichment source - see Map Enrichment Result notes.

nodes.name: Fetch Enrichment Result
nodes.notes: Dropcontact's real response shape (confirmed live, execution 93): a flat object at the top level ($json.email as an array of {email, qualification}), not the raw API's documented {data:[...]} wrapper - n8n's node unwraps data[0] before returning it.

nodes.name: Map Enrichment Result
nodes.notes: Defensive optional-chaining fallbacks because Dropcontact's real response shape is unverified - a wrong guess degrades to 'Failed/No Email Found' + Needs Review, not a crash. Raw Enrichment Response on the Airtable row preserves the untouched JSON for debugging.

value.Location: ={{$('Normalize Agent Output').item.json.location || $('Limit Results Per Criteria Row').item.json.criteria_location}}
value.Review Reason: ={{ !$json.enrichment_success ? 'Dropcontact enrichment did not return a verified email' : '' }}

nodes.name: Fetch Prospect Page
nodes.notes: v2 Phase B2': fetches whichever page SerpApi found (company site or third-party editorial mention) so the AI Agent can read real page text instead of just a 2-line snippet. responseFormat=text forces the raw HTML into $json.data for HTML Extract. Deliberately no auth - these are public third-party pages. onError continues gracefully since many sites will block bots or timeout; the Agent's existing 'null the name rather than guess' rule already handles a missing/thin page cleanly.

nodes.name: Parse Page Text
nodes.notes: v2 Phase B2': pulls visible body text from the fetched page. If the fetch failed or returned no HTML, this degrades to empty/missing page_text rather than erroring - the Agent already treats missing input as 'do not guess a name'. Known limitation: body-text extraction can include script/style noise and won't handle JS-rendered sites - flagged as an open risk to verify on first live test (Firecrawl is the fallback upgrade if this proves too noisy).

nodes.name: Has Company Domain?
nodes.notes: v2 Phase E': Hunter's emailFinder needs a domain to work with; if the AI Agent never found a company_website (common for an EditorialMention hit with no company site mentioned), skip straight to Dropcontact rather than calling Hunter with an empty domain.

nodes.name: Enrich Contact - Hunter
nodes.notes: v2 Phase E': runs first now that the pipeline reliably produces a real company domain (Dropcontact had none to work with in v1). Hunter's real response shape is unverified until a live execution is inspected - see Map Hunter Result notes for the defensive dual-shape guess.

nodes.name: Map Hunter Result
nodes.notes: v2 Phase E': Hunter's real response shape (flattened vs nested under 'data') is unverified until a live execution is inspected - both are checked defensively, same discipline as Map Enrichment Result's Dropcontact guess. Uses the same field names (enriched_email, enriched_phone, enrichment_success) as Map Enrichment Result so Create Prospect works identically regardless of which provider found the email. enrichment_source is for execution-log debugging only, not mapped to an Airtable column.

nodes.name: Limit - Companies Lane
nodes.notes: v2 fix: without a per-lane cap, whichever lane is ordered first into Merge Search Results wins 100% of the post-merge quota (confirmed live, executions 98-100) - each lane must be pre-limited so all 3 always contribute. Companies gets 40% of Max Results.

nodes.name: Limit - Editorial Lane
nodes.notes: v2 fix: same reasoning as Limit - Companies Lane. Editorial Mentions gets 40% of Max Results.

nodes.name: Limit - LinkedIn Lane
nodes.notes: v2 fix: same reasoning as Limit - Companies Lane. LinkedIn is demoted to 20% of Max Results (minimum 1) rather than 0%, since it occasionally does contribute a real find.

nodes.name: Normalize Agent Output

assignments.name: review_reason
assignments.value: ={{ $json.output ? ($json.output.review_reason || 'Low confidence / no identifiable prospect name') : 'AI extraction call failed (rate-limited or errored) - not evaluated, review source manually' }}

nodes.notes: Guards against Prospect Extraction Agent's output being entirely missing (Groq call failed all retries - confirmed live in execution 102). Without this, every downstream .output.X read silently resolved blank instead of surfacing the failure.
